questions.title: What is the difference between function declarations and expressions?
questions.answer: A function declaration defines a named function and can generally be called before its declaration in the same scope. A function expression creates a function as part of an expression and follows the initialization rules of its variable binding.
questions.underTheHood: Function declarations are initialized during environment setup. Function expressions are evaluated when execution reaches their expression.
pitfalls: Function expressions assigned to const cannot be accessed before initialization.
Function declarations and expressions have different initialization behavior.

questions.title: How do arrow functions differ from regular functions?
questions.answer: Arrow functions use lexical this, do not have their own arguments object, and cannot be used as constructors. Regular functions have their own this binding determined by how they are called.
questions.underTheHood: An arrow function captures this from its surrounding lexical environment rather than creating a new this binding during invocation.
pitfalls: Arrow functions are usually unsuitable as object methods that need dynamic this.
Arrow functions cannot be called with new.
call(), apply() and bind() cannot change an arrow function's lexical this.
followUps: Why can arrow functions not be constructors?
